**Element Layout (13.5 points):**
The split-screen layout effectively separates textual definitions from visual demonstrations. Text on the left is legible, though margins could be more generous. The right-side animation area is appropriately sized for geometry focus.

**Attractiveness (12.8 points):**
The neon-on-black aesthetic provides high contrast and a modern feel suitable for mathematical concepts. While minimalist, the clean vector-style animations maintain learner engagement without unnecessary distractions.

**Logic Flow (14.2 points):**
The progression is pedagogically strong, moving from fundamental 0D-3D construction to complex 4D concepts. Each section builds upon the previous, concluding with a practical application that reinforces the core knowledge point.

**Accuracy & Depth (14.5 points):**
Content is factually accurate regarding dimensional shifts and hypercube geometry. The explanation of a 4D tesseract unfolding into 3D cubes is a classic, correctly executed pedagogical tool for this topic.

**Visual Consistency (13.0 points):**
The video maintains a consistent formatting style and typographic hierarchy. Although the color palette shifts between segments, the line weights and animation timing remain uniform across the presentation.

**Overall Summary:**
This video provides a solid instructional sequence on dimensional geometry. It balances theoretical definitions with clear, synchronized visual metaphors. The scaffolding approach ensures the learner is prepared for the more complex hypercube and projection puzzles.

**Key Strengths:**
• Logical pedagogical scaffolding
• High-contrast visual design
• Effective use of unfolding animations

**Areas for Improvement:**
• Increase whitespace around text blocks
• Incorporate more varied visual textures
• Standardize color associations for specific axes

The volume of a cube is calculated by cubing its side length (V = s³). With a side length of 4, the volume is 4 x 4 x 4 = 64 cubic units.

C
A cube's faces are squares. A slice made by a plane parallel to one of these faces will produce a cross-section that is identical in shape and size to the face, which is a square.
